title: Class Factor Base Dyadic
objective: Compress exact primitive transcendental enclosures to outward dyadic intervals while preserving BDF certificates and improving cubic factor-base performance

handoff.summary: Exact primitive pi, logarithm, Euler-gamma, Catalan, and interval-log enclosures now retain their direct scalar-series oracle but cache a checked outward dyadic compression with 24 guard bits. The h=3 discriminant-minus1083 cubic keeps BDF bound 9, precision 64, the exact serialized margin, and the same five factor-base records while cold BDF selection falls from 2.31 seconds to about 0.85 seconds and warm fresh-field selection from 1.59 seconds to about 0.49 seconds. Differential tests cover scalar-versus-compressed containment at 32, 64, 96, and 128 bits and pin all existing representative BDF margins.
risks: The broad pnpm test:native lane gate reaches an unrelated exact-main inconsistency: test/dense-integer-migration.cjs forbids the lazy sagejs.kernels.matrix.dense_integer import that src/baselib/matrix.py already contains at base commit 01f0bdcc. Native FLINT, FFLAS, graph, M4RI, FFI, lifecycle, and production-kernel portions passed before that matrix-source assertion failed.

The task remains active because the mechanically required native receipt cannot pass without an out-of-scope matrix-lane correction. Focused factor-base, integrated engine, strict baselib, standalone Pyright, architecture, build, and benchmark checks pass.
next_steps: Central integration should resolve or update the dense-integer migration assertion and rerun pnpm test:native.
Do not broaden auto theorem selection from this change; corpus evidence should decide any later small-Minkowski cutoff.
